items.title: Bob Wilber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: Yeah, I played with Benny in the late ‘50s when he was putting together a band to go out on the road and I just went up and the word was out that Benny was auditioning up at this studio and I took my tenor and went up and he liked my playing.

ctx.x: You finally got to play with Benny Goodman in the ‘50s?

Yeah, I played with Benny in the late ‘50s when he was putting together a band to go out on the road and I just went up and the word was out that Benny was auditioning up at this studio and I took my tenor and went up and he liked my playing. So I did one tour and then I did another tour the next year, and I got to know Benny and he seemed to like me. I never got the ray, the famous Goodman ray. I didn’t get much chance to play clarinet in the band I must say, it was mostly tenor. But I developed a lifelong…
If you, for some strange reason, let’s suppose I was a doctor and gave you some advice, like you have to give up all your instruments except one. What would you choose?

items.title: Bob Wilber Interview, 1961-05-01
items.q: we used to play along with records, you know, Bob Crosby and Benny Goodman

ctx.x: And what kind of instrument was it? You know, metal ones or something like that, was it really?

Yeah, I had a Penzlmuller gold clarinet with silver keys and I thought that was much better, much flashier than the wooden ones, you know. Yeah. But I started to try to play jazz even, well maybe two or three years before that with, I had a buddy who was a drummer and I played a little tin flute and we used to play along with records, you know, Bob Crosby and Benny Goodman. A lot of the guys that did down here started on that.
Yeah. Yeah. At that time, who were your favorite musicians? Is that when you actually began playing?
